title: Finite-dimensionality of the section-induced scalar action on first additive cohomology
statement: Let f:C → Spec(k) be a smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field k [def-sc-curves]. Let G be a sheaf of abelian groups in coefficient universe u+1 on the small etale site, with natural additive equivalences a_U:G(U) ≃ Γ(U,O_U). Let T be first derived etale cohomology on sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Suppose m is a k-module structure on T(G), and for every c in k a sheaf endomorphism μ_c exists which multiplies sections under a_U by the pullback of c along U → C → Spec(k), and whose map on T(G) is multiplication by c for m. Then T(G), with this given action m, is finite-dimensional over k. There is no positive-characteristic, Frobenius, or surjectivity assertion.

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-proper-or-affine. For an affine curve, lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent makes first cohomology zero. For a proper curve use the natural etale/Zariski comparison on O_C and proper coherent cohomology finiteness. Naturality for scalar multiplication gives finite-dimensionality for the transported action. The assumed section formula uniquely determines each scalar sheaf map, so the comparison preserves the given module action m, rather than merely some abstract additive equivalence.

Compare the injective-resolution model naturally with derived global sections using lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification. For the larger coefficient universe compute with finite affine etale hypercovers: quasi-compactness supplies finite affine refinements, and lifting each finite cochain group identifies cocycles, boundaries, and scalar maps. Transport the Module structure, finiteness, and the scalar identities across these additive comparisons; no preservation of injectives by ULift is asserted.
